fi-centromochlus-perugiae.title: Honeycomb Tatia
fi-centromochlus-perugiae.summary: The oil catfish, Centromochlus perugiae, is a small auchenipterid catfish from Peru and Ecuador. It lives around the shorelines of swift-flowing rivers with sandy substrates and no aquatic plants. By…
rows: Insectivorous in the wild, but in aquaria it relishes live and frozen foods such as bloodworm, earthworms etc., as well as sinking dried foods.
notes: The fish like to squeeze themselves into spaces little bigger than themselves during the day, so provide plenty of hiding places among tangles of bogwood or lengths of plastic piping.
A sand substrate is best, and the fish prefer a good amount of water flow, although this isn't absolutely essential.

fi-megalechis-thoracata.title: Hoplo Catfish
fi-megalechis-thoracata.summary: The spotted hoplo, Megalechis thoracata, is a callichthyid catfish widespread across northern South America, living primarily in still waters. Still widely referred to as Hoplosternum thoracatum, it…
notes: The hoplo is not a particularly shy catfish but will still appreciate some cover in the form of rocks, plants and bogwood.
Water flow should be slow or still, although the fish will adapt to stronger conditions.

fi-oxydoras-niger.title: Ripsaw Catfish
fi-oxydoras-niger.summary: The ripsaw catfish, Oxydoras niger, is a large doradid catfish from many of the major river systems of northern South America. Reaching 90 cm, it is only for the experienced fishkeeper and best…
rows: Found throughout many of the major river systems of northern South America.
notes: Will appreciate cover in the form of rockwork, roots and bogwood.
Plants can also be used but ensure plenty swimming space is also provided.

fi-phractocephalus-hemioliopterus.title: Redtail Catfish
fi-phractocephalus-hemioliopterus.summary: The red-tail catfish, Phractocephalus hemioliopterus, is a giant pimelodid catfish from much of the Amazon and Rio Orinoco basins in South America. The largest specimen recorded by science measured…
rows: Carnivore / micropredator. Quite an opportunistic feeder in nature, feeding on fish, invertebrates and fallen fruits.
Present throughout much of the Amazon and Rio Orinoco basins in Colombia, Venezuela, Guyana, Ecuador, Peru, Bolivia and Brazil.
notes: Strictly speaking, decor isn't necessary for a tank containing an adult, provided the lighting is fairly dim.
You can however add some large chunks of bogwood, beech branches or smooth rocks if you wish.

fi-sorubim-lima.title: Lima Shovelnose Catfish
fi-sorubim-lima.summary: The duckbill catfish, Sorubim lima, is a pimelodid catfish recorded from rivers across South America, including the Amazon, Orinoco and Paraná. It is also known as the 'hockey stick catfish' and…
rows: Almost exclusively carnivorous preying on smaller fishes, crustaceans, invertebrates, etc.
A very widespread species that has been recorded from Venezuela, Ecuador, Colombia, Peru, Brazil, Bolivia, Paraguay, Uruguay and Argentina.
notes: This species is nocturnal and a dimly-lit tank with substrate of soft sand suits it best.
Other décor need consist only of some decent-sized roots and branches which can be arranged to form sheltered areas although plants can also be added should you wish.

fi-agamyxis-pectinifrons.title: Spotted Raphael Catfish
fi-agamyxis-pectinifrons.summary: The spotted talking catfish, Agamyxis pectinifrons, is a doradid catfish from the Amazon basin in Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia and Peru. Very common in the trade, it is hardy and relatively long-lived,…
rows: group of 4 or more specimens, though can be maintained individually if you wish, and it will also group together with similarly-looking relatives such as Platydoras armatulus, Acanthodoras spinosissimus, and Amblydoras hancockii.
Omnivore. This species is an omnivorous generalist and will accept most commonly-encountered prepared and frozen foods.
The type locality is given as 'Pebas, Equador' by Cope (1870), but this apparently refers to the settlement of the same name located east of the city of Iquitos in Loreto Region,…
notes: Best maintained in a dimly-lit set-up with a soft, sandy substrate and plenty of cover in the form of aquatic vegetation, tangles of driftwood or artificial caves of some kind.
Bright lighting isn't really appreciated since this species is largely nocturnal by nature.

fi-liosomadoras-morrowi.title: False Jaguar Catfish
fi-liosomadoras-morrowi.summary: The false jaguar catfish, Liosomadoras morrowi, is an auchenipterid catfish from the Río Ucayali basin in Peru. It is often confused with its congener L. oncinus, from which it differs in its duller…
notes: This is a nocturnal fish, so dim lighting is required to make it feel secure.
Plenty of cover should also be provided, particularly if you're keeping several fish together.

fi-pimelodus-pictus.title: Polka Dot Pictus Catfish
fi-pimelodus-pictus.summary: The pictus cat, Pimelodus pictus, is a small pimelodid catfish from the Rio Orinoco and Amazon basins in Colombia, Venezuela, Peru and Brazil. The most popular member of the genus in the hobby, it is…
rows: Schooling / social — keep a proper group
Native to the Rio Orinoco and Amazon basins in Colombia, Venezuela, Peru and Brazil.
notes: Does best in a dimly lit environment with plenty of swimming space, and a few hiding places to provide security.
You won't see it move around as much in a brightly lit tank, except perhaps at feeding time.

fi-pseudoplatystoma-fasciatum.title: Tiger Shovelnose Catfish
fi-pseudoplatystoma-fasciatum.summary: The barred shovelnose, Pseudoplatystoma fasciatum, is a large pimelodid catfish with a very wide range in South America, from Colombia to Argentina. Recorded at 104 cm and 70 kg, it reaches close to…
rows: Predator / carnivore. Piscivorous by nature, but usually adapts well to dead foods in captivity.
Has a very wide natural range.
notes: Strictly speaking, decor isn't necessary for a tank containing an adult, provided the lighting is fairly dim.
You can however add some large chunks of bogwood, beech branches or smooth rocks if you wish.

fi-anadoras-grypus.title: Speckled Talking Catfish
fi-anadoras-grypus.summary: Anadoras grypus is a species of thorny catfish found in the upper Amazon basin of Ecuador, Peru, Colombia, and Bolivia. [ 1 ] [ 2 ] This species grows to a length of 14.6 centimetres (5.7 in) SL. [ 3 ]
rows: Up to about 14.6 cm SL male/unsexed (FishBase max)

fi-microglanis-iheringi.title: Bumblebee Catfish
fi-microglanis-iheringi.summary: Microglanis iheringi is a species of South American catfish described by Alcides Lourenço Gomes in 1945. [ 1 ] The species belongs to the genus Microglanis, a group of catfishes that are native to…
rows: Up to about 6.0 cm SL male/unsexed (FishBase max)

fi-pimelodus-blochii.title: Four Line Pictus Catfish
fi-pimelodus-blochii.summary: Pimelodus blochii, commonly the Bloch's catfish [ 3 ] [ 4 ] is a fish in the family Pimelodidae. [ 5 ] [ 6 ]
rows: Up to about 35.0 cm TL male/unsexed (FishBase max)

fi-sturisoma-aureum.title: Royal Farlowella Catfish
fi-sturisoma-aureum.summary: Sturisomatichthys aureus is a species of freshwater ray-finned fish belonging to the family Loricariidae, the suckermouth armored catfishes, and the subfamily Loricariinae, the mailed catfishes. […
rows: Up to about 20.0 cm SL male/unsexed (FishBase max)

fi-rineloricaria-fallax.title: Whiptail Loricaria Catfish
fi-rineloricaria-fallax.summary: One of the most common whiptail catfish in the trade: a flat, leaf-litter catfish from Guyana and Brazil that is very peaceful and breeds fairly readily in caves.
rows: Very peaceful; easily outcompeted at feeding time
Best kept in a small group
Omnivore. Sinking foods, blanched vegetables (spinach, zucchini, kale) and frozen bloodworm or daphnia
Upper Rupununi and Branco river basins, Guyana and Brazil
notes: Sand with a layer of dried leaves and some wood suits it; avoid very bright light.
Offer caves or narrow tubes: the female lays eggs inside and the male guards them.

fi-platydoras-armatulus.title: Striped Raphael Catfish
fi-platydoras-armatulus.sci: Platydoras armatulus (often sold as P. costatus)
fi-platydoras-armatulus.summary: A hardy, armored "talking" catfish with a bold cream stripe running down a chocolate-brown body. It makes audible croaking sounds with its pectoral spines and spends the day tucked into cover, coming out to forage after dark.
rows: About 9 in (240 mm) standard length (SL) in aquariums (Seriously Fish); FishBase lists a 43 cm SL wild record
Not aggressive at all, but it swallows fish small enough to fit in its mouth; keep it with species too big to be food
Tolerates its own kind; a group often shares one hiding place
Omnivore and easy to feed: sinking pellets or tablets as the staple, plus live or frozen bloodworm, small earthworms and similar. Feed after lights out
Widespread in South America: Orinoco basin, Guianas coastal rivers and much of the Amazon basin south to the Tocantins and Parnaíba (Seriously Fish)
notes: Give dim lighting and plenty of caves, pipes or tangled driftwood; it becomes bolder as it grows. A red night light lets you watch it feed.
Handle with care: the pectoral spines and small body spines snag easily in nets.

fi-rineloricaria-l010a.title: Red Lizard Whiptail Catfish (L010a)
fi-rineloricaria-l010a.summary: A slim, flat red-brown whiptail catfish that rests on sand and wood. One of the most peaceful catfish around and easy to keep in a calm community.
rows: About 30 × 12 in footprint (~18 gal) for a small group
Can be kept in small groups
Omnivore: sinking foods, blanched vegetables (spinach, zucchini, kale) and frozen bloodworm or daphnia
Unclear: may be a man-made aquarium variety; whiptails come from South America
notes: Give it a sand bottom, leaf litter and some wood or rock caves.
Avoid boisterous tankmates that outcompete it for food.

fi-farlowella-twig-catfish.title: Twig Catfish (Farlowella)
fi-farlowella-twig-catfish.summary: A very thin, stick-shaped catfish that grazes algae on wood and plants. Peaceful but delicate: it needs spotless, well-oxygenated water and lots of vegetable food.
rows: Mostly vegetarian: cucumber, kale, blanched spinach, algae wafers and spirulina tablets, with occasional bloodworm or daphnia
Moderate: very sensitive to poor water
South America (F. acus was described from near Caracas, Venezuela)
notes: Needs well-oxygenated water with some current, dim light and plenty of driftwood.
Easily outcompeted for food by larger or faster fish.
warn: Very sensitive to poor water quality: keep up with water changes.

fi-centromochlus-musaica.title: Ninja Woodcat
fi-centromochlus-musaica.sci: Centromochlus musaica (also listed as Tatia musaica)
fi-centromochlus-musaica.summary: A small, boldly marked driftwood catfish from Venezuela that hides by day and comes out at dusk. Peaceful in groups, but it will eat very small fish and fry.
rows: Peaceful; adults eat very tiny fish and fry
Catfish pellets, granules, flake and frozen foods; bloodworm tempts it out
notes: Mostly nocturnal: give it plenty of hiding places and dim lighting.

fi-shovelnose-hybrid-redtail-tiger.title: Redtail × Tiger Shovelnose Hybrid Catfish
fi-shovelnose-hybrid-redtail-tiger.summary: A man-made hybrid of two giant South American catfish. It grows huge and eats any fish it can swallow, so it is only for owners with very large tanks or ponds.
rows: Very large: the redtail parent reaches about 5 ft 11 in (1.8 m) and the tiger shovelnose parent about 35 in (90 cm)
Full-grown redtail catfish need about 2,600 gal (10,000 L); plan on a very large tank or pond
Predatory; eats any fish that fits in its mouth
Carnivore: fish, shrimp and other meaty foods
Man-made hybrid; parents come from the Amazon and other South American river basins
warn: Grows far too big for normal home aquariums. Plan for a very large tank or pond before buying.
